paper_metadata.title: Achieving enhanced strength retention at elevated temperatures in ultrafine-fibrous interconnected Al–Ce–Ni eutectic alloy solidified under super-gravity field
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: Al–Ce–Ni ternary eutectic alloy was chosen as a modal system, which was reported for the first time to be solidified under super-gravity field
The three-phase eutectics in Al – Ce – Ni alloy solidified under super- gravity conditions exhibits a fine fibrous wall structure with more than 21 “ chains ” .

The size of eutectic colonies in the core regions of S1, S2 and S3 alloys are ~29.6 μm, ~25.8 μm, and ~24.9 μm respectively, while the size of eutectic colonies in S0 is ~89.7 μm.

the fibrous arrangement of the Al(A)-Al11Ce3(B)–Al3Ni(C) three-phase eutectic structure presents a pattern of ABCA, ABA, ACA, or ABCBA. Interestingly, more complex ABCBC…BCA spatial arrangement with finer fibers is detected in S3.
Coarse Al11Ce3 and Al3Ni eutectic phases can be identified around the eutectic colony boundaries in sample S0, indicated by blue and red arrows respectively (see Fig. 4 b).
Coarse primary phases can be observed in the peripheral region of the S0 sample (~35%), as indicated by purple arrows in Fig. 2 e and f.
Porosities are easily noted in the S0 sample, as highlighted by yellow arrows in Fig. 2 a, in contrast to the S3 sample, where porosity is significantly reduced (demonstrated in Fig. 2 b).
certain micro-cracks are detected in either coarse Al11Ce3 or Al3Ni eutectic phase, which are highlighted by yellow arrows in eutectic colony boundaries (Fig. 9 a).
Several voids are visible in fracture surface of S0 with numerous shallow dimples and tearing ridges.

In our work, it is noted that lamellar Al11Ce3 are present in the S0 sample (as shown in Fig. 4a), whereas morphology was transferred from lamellar to fibrous structure within the eutectic colony of S3.

Noted that the three-phase eutectic structure in S3 is spatially interconnected through the extensive fibrous formation of Al3Ni (Fig. 6e), resulting in the formation of an ultrafine fibrous interconnected structure (maked by white arrows).

Thus, it is reasonable to conclude that the nucleation rate of ternary eutectics in S3 were significantly enhanced, creating conditions for the cooperative growth of the ternary eutectics to form the ultrafine-fibrous interconnected structure.
Certain pores could be detected in S0 sample. The main cracks (marked by dotted red line in Fig. 8) preferred to originate either in pores or coarse two-phase regions.

Multiple micro-cracks were detected on and beneath the fracture surface, which were highlighted by yellow arrows in Figs. 8 and 9.
A large number of deep dimples and tearing edges were observed in fracture surface, as provided in Fig. 8h.

evidence.quote: Fig. 12 shows the changes in the Vickers microhardness of the S0 and S3 alloy samples after 48 h of heat exposure. The hardness of both samples decreased in the first 6 h, remained stable after 12 h, with a total reduction of 6.1 % and 10.6 %, respectively.
the formation of ultrafine-fibrous interconnected Al11Ce3–Al3Ni eutectic clusters with more “chains” and higher spatial connectivity was detected mainly due to the relatively higher nucleation rate
super-gravity field was reported to strongly intensify the buoyancy-driven flow of liquid during solidification [25, 26], affecting the solute convection and morphology of eutectic structure

the nucleation and growth of eutectic structure might be affected by the reduced differences in composition of the liquid phase and enhancement of the mass transfer during super-gravity solidification

mechanisms.name: Gibbs free energy of nucleation reduction

evidence.quote: super-gravity field may lead to the reduction in Gibbs free energy of nucleation, which was affected by gravity coefficient.
